key_idea: The proof encodes 'no stably properly infinite matrix algebra' as a topological obstruction: a nonvanishing top Chern class of bundles over products of projective spaces. Finite propagation of shift-like generators means that, by degree truncation, a polynomial approximation to a pair of orthogonal isometries would give a forbidden trivial subbundle. A telescoping diagonal construction then turns the strict row/column norm gap into a uniform quasitrace additivity defect.
reason: Theorem 7 rests on a striking, reusable idea, and Lemma 8 is a short telescoping gem: degree-bounded polynomials see only finitely many levels, so a vector-bundle Chern-class obstruction applies. The bundle construction in Proposition 6, however, carries considerable numerical bookkeeping (multiplicities divided by four, sizing the projective-space factors, two families of maps, incidence-dimension estimates), and that weighs on economy and simplicity.
